summary: ROUTED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR to the events lane as EVENTS-006, which is now active. The analysis below is the events lane EVENTS-005 measurement and is unchanged; the orchestrator opened the bounded task and dispatched it rather than absorbing the behaviour change into its own board work. This is the ONE open item in HF-DB023-EVENT-POSTS-CALLERS' completion condition that EVENTS-005 did not close, and it is raised here rather than absorbed, because the fix is a behaviour change to a public launch surface and EVENTS-005's six acceptance criteria do not name it. THE QUESTION, ANSWERED AS FAR AS IT CAN BE. `event_posts_visibility_read` (installed by 20260928010000) is `visibility = 'public' OR auth.uid() = user_id` with NO predicate on the parent event's publication state, and `anon` holds SELECT. So a public-visibility post attached to an unpublished event is readable through PostgREST by anyone holding the anon key who knows the event id. WHY NO DATABASE POLICY CAN CLOSE IT, MEASURED IN THE MIGRATION THAT INSTALLED IT. A publication predicate must branch on three parent relations (`public.events`, `public.artist_events`, `public.events_v2`), so it is three subqueries in one policy. 20260928010000's own header records the measured consequence: a policy `OR` containing a subplan over a table the evaluating role cannot read fails the WHOLE query with 42501, because a table-level ACL is checked when the subplan node runs, not per row and not per disjunct. `anon` holds no SELECT on any of the three event tables, so a publication predicate in the read policy would make EVERY anonymous read of an event post fail 42501 -- a launch outage on the public event page, and the exact failure the migration avoided by splitting its attendees arm into a role-scoped policy. The transcribable form therefore does not exist for the `anon` role, and the policy DB-023 installed is the correct schema-side posture for a file that does not own the event publication contract. THE RESIDUAL IS REACHABLE, AND HERE IS THE PATH. `components/events/enhanced-event-page.tsx:120` reads `public.event_posts` through the BROWSER client, and `lib/supabase/client.ts:13` is the anon key. That read is filtered only on `(event_id, event_table = 'events')` and carries no publication check. It is reached from `app/events/[slug]/page.tsx` with no auth gate, so the exposure is a public-visibility post on a DRAFT legacy `events` row being readable by anyone who knows the event id. Both API readers are already gated -- `app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts` and `app/api/events/[id]/page/route.ts` both call `canAccessEventAsViewer`, and EVENTS-005 kept and pinned both gates with a test, because a now-existing RLS policy is not a reason to remove the application gate. THE FIX IS SMALL AND IS NOT IN THIS TASK. `loadEventPosts` already does its own read plus its own `fetchProfilesByIds` hydration; routing it through `GET /api/events/[id]/posts` reuses the gate AND deletes a duplicate profile-hydration derivation, so it is a simplification of the component rather than an expansion. EVENTS-005 did not do it because AC-2 names the WRITE specifically, the read change alters loading and error behaviour on a public surface with no stated criterion, and a task that quietly widens past its own acceptance criteria is exactly the failure the events charter warns about.

No further action on the publication-state question at the application layer: the only product reader of public.event_posts now goes through a canAccessEventAsViewer gate, and neither API gate was removed. A now-existing RLS policy is not a reason to remove an application gate, and the test suite now fails if either route stops calling canAccessEventAsViewer.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, restated because it is the part that is easy to lose: the installed event_posts_visibility_read policy STILL has no predicate on the parent event's publication state, and anon STILL holds SELECT on public.event_posts. The surface is closed at the application layer only. That is deliberate and measured — a publication predicate cannot exist for the anon role without making every anonymous read of an event post fail 42501 — so do not file a request for one. The four test cases in __tests__/events/event-posts-anon-read-closure.test.ts assert this residual state, so a green run cannot be misread as schema-level closure.
